page: OVHcloud t1-le-90 is a GPU-accelerated server instance within the Cloud GPU family, utilizing the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon Silver 4214 processor running at 3.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 90.0 GB of system memory, providing 5.62 GB per core. For hardware acceleration, it bundles two NVIDIA V100 GPUs based on the Volta architecture, delivering a combined 32 GB of VRAM. Local storage consists of a 400 GB NVMe SSD, and network connectivity is rated at a 4 Gbps baseline.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance split between single-core and multi-core workloads. Single-core CPU performance is positioned in the bottom 25% tier, as shown by stress-ng and Geekbench single-core tests. However, multi-core performance scales to average levels, supported by the 16 dedicated physical cores. Memory bandwidth is average for large block reads and writes, though the overall Passmark memory score falls into the lower quartile.

The primary strength of this server lies in its GPU-accelerated capabilities, particularly for machine learning workloads. LLM inference benchmarks show top-tier performance for prompt processing and text generation on small to medium models, such as the 135M and 7B parameter architectures. This makes the instance highly cost-efficient for deep learning inference, parallel data processing, and GPU-bound rendering tasks, whereas it is less suited for single-threaded CPU-bound applications.
description: The OVHcloud t1-le-90 is a KVM-based server in the Cloud GPU family, designed for workloads requiring hardware acceleration. It features 16 dedicated physical cores from an Intel Xeon Silver 4214 processor running at 3.0 GHz, paired with 90.0 GB of RAM and a 400 GB NVMe SSD. The server's primary performance driver is its dual NVIDIA V100 GPU configuration, providing a total of 32 GB of VRAM. While single-core CPU and memory benchmarks place the instance in the lower performance tiers, its multi-core capabilities are average, and its GPU-driven LLM inference performance for small and medium models reaches top-tier levels. This hardware profile makes the t1-le-90 highly suitable for machine learning inference, parallel data processing, and graphics rendering, offering a balanced resource density for GPU-centric tasks.
